overview: The APEDA Agri Export Promotion Scheme is a financial assistance program designed to support exporters of scheduled agricultural and processed food products. It provides financial assistance for activities such as market development, quality development, and export infrastructure development under the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26). The scheme aims to enhance India's agri-export competitiveness through targeted interventions in key product segments.
objectives: Collection and publication of export statistics
Training in various aspects of connected industries
Improvement of packaging and marketing of scheduled products outside India
eligibility: Exporters of APEDA-scheduled products who are registered with APEDA and possess a valid Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the scheme. Applicants must submit a detailed project proposal along with supporting documents including IEC code, MSME registration (if applicable), GST and PAN details, audited financials, and other category-specific documentation as outlined in the application guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance for export promotion activities including market development, quality upgradation, and infrastructure development. Non-financial benefits include access to APEDA's market intelligence, participation in international trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and technical support for compliance with international standards. The scheme also facilitates registration, certification, and export facilitation services.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as a subsidy based on the nature and scope of the project, subject to approval by the competent authority. The quantum of support is determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the activity type, beneficiary profile, and alignment with scheme objectives. Funds are disbursed in installments linked to project milestones and subject to submission of utilization certificates and audited expenditure statements.
application_process: 1. Visit the APEDA website and navigate to the Financial Assistance Schemes section. 2. Download the scheme guidelines and application form for the specific component (Market Development, Quality Development, or Export Infrastructure Development). 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Gather required documents such as IEC code, RCMC, MSME registration (if applicable), GST/PAN details, audited financials, and category-specific documents. 5. Submit the completed application along with supporting documents via the designated portal or email. 6. Await scrutiny and evaluation by APEDA officials. 7. If approved, receive Registration-cum-Allocation Certificate (RCAC) or equivalent approval. 8. Implement the project as per the approved plan. 9. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 10. Undergo final inspection and submit final report for closure and final disbursement.
required_documents: Audited or provisional financials for FY 2024–25
Certifications, Awards, or GI-tagged product mentions (if applicable)
Production or processing facilities (with photos if relevant)
Quality certifications and compliance (Global GAP, ISO, HACCP, USDA Organic, NPOP etc.)
Financial Snapshot: Revenue, EBITDA, and Profit (FY 2023-24 & provisional FY 2024-25)
Trade Partnerships, Buyers, or Distribution Channels
Reason for applying to the Bharati Acceleration programme
Contact Details: Name, designation, phone, email, and office address
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per the scheme window (2021-22 to 2025-26).
implementing_agency: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
caveats: Financial assistance is subject to availability of funds and approval by the competent authority.
Beneficiaries must maintain proper records and submit utilization certificates and audited expenditure statements.
The scheme is operational only during the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26).
Applicants must ensure that the proposed activity aligns with APEDA's scheduled products and export promotion objectives.
Submission of false information or documents may lead to rejection and blacklisting.
